text.opengl: Load `heightmap.png` with stb_image (keep its width, height and number of channels) and print its size; if it cannot be loaded, print an error and end the program.
text.vulkan: In `loadHeightMap()`, load the height map with stb_image (keep its width, height and number of channels) and print its size; if it cannot be loaded, throw an error.
text.d3d12: Load `heightmap.png` with stb_image (keep its width, height and number of channels); if it cannot be loaded, throw an error. Write its size to the debugger's output.

hint.opengl: `unsigned char *data = stbi_load("heightmap.png", &width, &height, &nrChannels, 0);` – 0 asks for the file's own channels (1 here). Print `"Loaded heightmap of size " << height << " x " << width`. Do not free `data` yet: the next task reads the pixels.
hint.vulkan: `unsigned char* data = stbi_load(path, &width, &height, &nrChannels, 0);` – 0 asks for the file's own channels (1 here). `if (!data) { throw std::runtime_error("failed to load height map!"); }`, then `std::cout << "Loaded heightmap of size " << height << " x " << width << std::endl;`. Do not free `data` yet: the next task reads the pixels.
hint.d3d12: `unsigned char* data = stbi_load("heightmap.png", &width, &height, &nrChannels, 0);` – 0 asks for the file's own channels (1 here). `snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "Loaded heightmap of size %d x %d\n", height, width); OutputDebugStringA(text);`. Do not free `data` yet: the next task reads the pixels.

text.opengl: Make one vertex per pixel: x from the column, z from the row (both centred around 0), y from the pixel's grey value scaled by 64/256 and shifted down by 16. Free the image, put the vertices into a VBO with a VAO (attribute 0: three floats), and for now draw them as points.
text.vulkan: Make one vertex per pixel: x from the column, z from the row (both centred around 0), y from the pixel's grey value scaled by 64/256 and shifted down by 16; free the image. Create the vertex buffer from them, and for now draw the vertices as points.
text.d3d12: Make one vertex per pixel: x from the column, z from the row (both centred around 0), y from the pixel's grey value scaled by 64/256 and shifted down by 16. Free the image, put the vertices into a vertex buffer with its view, and for now draw them as points.

hint.opengl: The pixel at row `i`, column `j` starts at `data + (j + width * i) * bytePerPixel`; its first byte is the height. `vertices.push_back(-width / 2.0f + width * j / (float)width);` (x), `(int)y * yScale - yShift` (y), `-height / 2.0f + height * i / (float)height` (z). Draw: `glDrawArrays(GL_POINTS, 0, (GLsizei)(vertices.size() / 3));`.
hint.vulkan: The pixel at row `i`, column `j` starts at `data + (j + width * i) * bytePerPixel`; its first byte is the height. `vertex.pos.x = -width / 2.0f + width * j / (float) width;`, `vertex.pos.y = (int) y * yScale - yShift;`, `vertex.pos.z = -height / 2.0f + height * i / (float) height;`, `vertices.push_back(vertex);`. Call `createVertexBuffer();` after `loadHeightMap(…)` in `initVulkan()`. Points: `inputAssembly.topology = VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_POINT_LIST;`, and the vertex shader must write `gl_PointSize = 1.0;` (Vulkan draws points only with a size from the shader). In `recordCommandBuffer()`: `vkCmdBindVertexBuffers` and `vkCmdDraw(commandBuffer, static_cast<uint32_t>(vertices.size()), 1, 0, 0);`.
hint.d3d12: The pixel at row `i`, column `j` starts at `data + (j + width * i) * bytePerPixel`; its first byte is the height. `vertices.push_back(-width / 2.0f + width * j / (float)width);` (x), `(int)y * yScale - yShift` (y), `-height / 2.0f + height * i / (float)height` (z). Keep the count: `m_vertexCount = static_cast<UINT>(vertices.size() / 3);`. In `PopulateCommandList`: `IASetPrimitiveTopology(D3D_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_POINTLIST)`, `IASetVertexBuffers`, `DrawInstanced(m_vertexCount, 1, 0, 0)` – the PSO is already made for points.

text.opengl: Build the index buffer for triangle strips: for every pair of neighbouring rows, one strip that zigzags between them (`j + width * i`, `j + width * (i + 1)` for each column j). Count the strips and their triangles, and put the indices into an element buffer bound to the VAO.
text.vulkan: Build the indices of the triangle strips: for every pair of neighbouring rows, one strip that zigzags between them (`j + width * i`, `j + width * (i + 1)` for each column j). Count the strips and their triangles, print the numbers, and create the index buffer.
text.d3d12: Build the index buffer for triangle strips: for every pair of neighbouring rows, one strip that zigzags between them (`j + width * i`, `j + width * (i + 1)` for each column j). Count the strips and their triangles, write them to the debugger's output, and put the indices into an index buffer with its view.

hint.opengl: learnopengl's three loops: `for (int i = 0; i < height - 1; i += rez) for (int j = 0; j < width; j += rez) for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) indices.push_back(j + width * (i + k * rez));` with `rez = 1`; `numStrips = (height - 1) / rez`, `numTrisPerStrip = (width / rez) * 2 - 2`. Bind the IBO while the VAO is bound.
hint.vulkan: learnopengl's three loops: `for (int i = 0; i < height - 1; i += rez) for (int j = 0; j < width; j += rez) for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) indices.push_back(j + width * (i + k * rez));` with `int rez = 1;`; `numStrips = (height - 1) / rez;`, `numTrisPerStrip = (width / rez) * 2 - 2;`. Call `createIndexBuffer();` after `createVertexBuffer();`.
hint.d3d12: learnopengl's three loops: `for (int i = 0; i < height - 1; i += rez) for (int j = 0; j < width; j += rez) for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) indices.push_back(j + width * (i + k * rez));` with `rez = 1`; `m_numStrips = (height - 1) / rez`, `m_numTrisPerStrip = (width / rez) * 2 - 2`. The view's format is `DXGI_FORMAT_R32_UINT`.

text.opengl: Draw the terrain as triangle strips instead of points: one `glDrawElements` per strip, each starting at its own offset in the index buffer.
text.vulkan: Draw the terrain as triangle strips instead of points: bind the index buffer and record one indexed draw per strip, each starting at its own first index.
text.d3d12: Draw the terrain as triangle strips instead of points: make the PSO draw triangles, set the strip topology and the index buffer, and record one indexed draw per strip, each starting at its own place in the index buffer.

hint.opengl: `glDrawElements(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, numTrisPerStrip + 2, GL_UNSIGNED_INT, (void*)(sizeof(unsigned int) * (numTrisPerStrip + 2) * strip));` in a loop over `strip` – a strip of n triangles has n + 2 indices.
hint.vulkan: `inputAssembly.topology = VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_STRIP;` (and the vertex shader no longer needs `gl_PointSize`). `vkCmdBindIndexBuffer(commandBuffer, indexBuffer, 0, VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT32);`, then `for (int strip = 0; strip < numStrips; strip++) vkCmdDrawIndexed(commandBuffer, numTrisPerStrip + 2, 1, (numTrisPerStrip + 2) * strip, 0, 0);` – a strip of n triangles has n + 2 indices.
hint.d3d12: `psoDesc.PrimitiveTopologyType = D3D12_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TYPE_TRIANGLE;` (strips are triangles too), `IASetPrimitiveTopology(D3D_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLESTRIP)`, `IASetIndexBuffer(&m_indexBufferView)`, and `DrawIndexedInstanced(m_numTrisPerStrip + 2, 1, (m_numTrisPerStrip + 2) * strip, 0, 0);` in a loop over `strip` – a strip of n triangles has n + 2 indices.

text.opengl: Colour the terrain by its height: in the fragment shader shift and scale the height (-16 … 48) into a grey value from 0 to 1.
text.vulkan: Colour the terrain by its height: in the fragment shader shift and scale the height (-16 … 48) into a grey value from 0 to 1.
text.d3d12: Colour the terrain by its height: in the pixel shader shift and scale the height (-16 … 48) into a grey value from 0 to 1.

hint.opengl: `float h = (Height + 16.0) / 64.0; FragColor = vec4(h, h, h, 1.0);` – the vertex shader already passes `Height = aPos.y`.
hint.vulkan: `float h = (Height + 16.0) / 64.0; outColor = vec4(h, h, h, 1.0);` – the vertex shader already passes `Height = inPosition.y`.
hint.d3d12: `float h = (input.height + 16.0f) / 64.0f; return float4(h, h, h, 1.0f);` – the vertex shader already passes `result.height = position.y`.
